D023_l001.question:
A 48-year-old married male civil servant presents with a 1 year and 2 month history of recurrent episodes of markedly increased food intake. During these episodes, the patient consumes quantities of food clearly exceeding typical portions for comparable situations within a limited time frame and reports a subjective inability to reduce or stop eating once started, with diminished control over both amount and type of food consumed.

Episodes are characterized by markedly accelerated eating pace and occur even in the absence of physiological hunger, with intake initiated and continued despite feeling physically replete. The patient describes consuming substantially more than intended and feeling unable to delay or interrupt the behavior.

Following these episodes, he experiences pronounced negative affect, including self-directed disgust, prominent guilt, and low mood related specifically to the eating behavior. The binge episodes have occurred, on average, at least once weekly for a period exceeding 3 months and have led to significant psychological distress. There is no report of regular compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise.
D023_l001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
